title: How do we draw acute and obtuse angles in different directions?
description: A paper corner is the guide for drawing a few acute angles and a few obtuse angles, and the page is turned to draw each kind in a new direction. The check lays the corner on every drawing to confirm its kind.
teaching_notes: One idea: the kind of an angle depends on its opening, not on the way it points. Watch for children who think a turned angle becomes a different kind.

video_script.why: The child draws acute and obtuse angles by comparing the opening with a right angle, and sees that turning the page keeps the kind.
video_script.substitution: A paper corner as the guide, and a page that is turned to draw in new directions.
video_script.anchor: a sheet of paper with a paper corner as the guide for the openings
video_script.payoff_line: Angles smaller than a right angle are acute. Angles between a right angle and a straight angle are obtuse. Both can point in any direction.

final_answer.value: acute angles are smaller than a right angle; obtuse angles are bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight angle; each can be drawn turned in any direction
final_answer.spoken: acute angles are smaller than a right angle, obtuse angles are between a right angle and a straight angle, and both can point in any direction

hold_back: acute = smaller than a right angle
obtuse = between a right angle and a straight angle
maths_rules: acute: opening smaller than the paper corner, less than a quarter turn
obtuse: opening wider than the paper corner but short of a straight line, more than a quarter turn and less than a half turn
turning the page changes the direction of the arms but not the opening, so the kind stays the same
video_script.design: One sheet and one amber corner stay on the board. The sheet is turned once for each kind, and the corner is laid on every drawing in the check.
